title: CAUTION Go presentation-versus-rule semantics
decision: RESOLUTION B — the Appendix C §C.4 line 791 statement governs presentation of a rule-generated Go advisory, not automatic emission of Go conditioned on S = CAUTION.

formal_semantics.asserts: S = CAUTION  ∧  Go ∈ AI(E)   →   Present(Go, caution_qualifier)

P2_rule_availability.note: Batch 2 RS_candidate(CAUTION) contains no Go rules; GAP-03 records the absence of scientific evidence

P4_advisory_generation.note: treated as a precondition of Interpretation B, not an entailment of line 791

P5_automatic_presentation.formal: system attaches caution qualifier to Go when presented
P5_automatic_presentation.reading: presentation-layer attribute (reading b), not automatic emission (reading a)

evidence_basis: appendix-c-formalisation.md line 791 continuation: 'The recommendation type remains Go, but its presentation and explanation are modified by the safety state. This preserves set containment while allowing state-dependent advisory messaging.' — presentation-layer framing.

architecture-illustration.md lines 202–204 (parallel canonical text): does not use the word 'automatically'; frames the qualifier as messaging ('communicates', 'understands'); explicitly labels the subsection 'Why Go carries a caution qualifier in CAUTION mode'.

architecture-illustration.md line 137 (governance table CAUTION cell): 'Go/no-go with caution qualifier, delay guidance' — corroborating presentation-level evidence that Go-related advice under CAUTION carries a caution qualifier. The informal phrase 'Go/no-go' is prose, not a formal enumeration of R types; R = {Go, Delay, DepartureTime, Duration} is unchanged and contains no 'No-go' element.
appendix-c-formalisation.md §C.7.1: rule engine fires only rules present in RS(S); structural constraint before generation, no post-hoc filtering. Denies the mechanism required by Interpretation A.
justification-layer3-enforcement.md §3–§4 (commit f517fc1, 2026-04-25): explicit rejection of post-hoc generation; proof by construction based on rule-set contents only.
Journal 1 Algorithm Specification batch 4 §11: Algorithm 4 wrapper is 'check G(S); if 0 → return ∅; else → invoke engine.reason(E, RS(S))' — no third emission branch.

recommendation-semantics-batch2.csv Go row: 'The rule system found no active Delay antecedent in the resolved environmental inputs.' — Batch 2 defines Go as a rule-based negative-existential conclusion, not an S-conditional emission.

rule-candidate-register-batch2.csv R-REJ-002: 'IF S == CAUTION THEN Delay' rejected as 'state-restatement without independent evidence' — pattern precedent applies to any hypothetical 'IF S == CAUTION THEN Go' rule.

scientific-gap-register-batch2.csv GAP-03: 'No evidence in the repository for recommending a Go advisory within CAUTION state.' The cited fisher studies (Rahim, Gao, Yamin) report behavioural patterns which Batch 2 mapped, through explicit architectural and advisory-mapping inference bridges, toward restricted-operation or Delay analogues (see rule-candidate-register-batch2.csv mapping_bridge_source fields). Those studies are not treated here as directly defining the canonical CAUTION → Delay AI advisory mapping.

closure-batch2.json: line 791 already classified as B (UI/presentation guidance) as the working interpretation; OPEN-L3-3 opened only because the surface word 'automatically' left the wording readable as A.

Provenance chronology: line 791 introduced 2026-04-10 (c42aae6c); the Layer 3 rule-based enforcement mechanism was decided 2026-04-25 (f517fc1) — line 791 predates the enforcement mechanism by 15 days but was retained through 8 subsequent §C.4 revisions with the same content. Retention through later revisions is consistent with continued treatment as presentation guidance, particularly when read alongside the clearer parallel canonical wording in architecture-illustration.md §202–204; retention alone is not treated here as proof of conscious reinterpretation.

reasons: No canonical or algorithm-level authority specifies a Go emission mechanism outside the rule engine.
§C.7.1 explicitly denies post-hoc generation; Layer 3 justification §3 explicitly denies output filtering.
Algorithm 4 has no branch for automatic Go emission.
A rule-based instantiation of A would require an 'IF S == CAUTION THEN Go' rule structurally identical to REJECTED R-REJ-002.
Batch 2 gap-register GAP-03 records zero empirical evidence for a CAUTION Go rule; three independent fisher studies (Rahim, Gao, Yamin) map CAUTION-equivalent conditions to Delay behavioural analog.
Task §20 stop condition: resolution must not require inventing a CAUTION-Go rule.

Line 791 was retained through multiple subsequent §C.4 revisions; retention is consistent with continued treatment as presentation guidance rather than obsolescence, though retention alone is not treated as proof of conscious reinterpretation.
The parallel statement in architecture-illustration.md §202 restates the same content with clearer presentation-layer wording, further indicating retention as presentation guidance.
No downstream authority explicitly supersedes line 791.

canonical_effect.appendix_c_status: MINIMAL CLARIFICATION PROPOSED (not automatically applied — see canonical_change_proposal below)

canonical_change_proposal.old_wording: When S = CAUTION, the **Go** recommendation is automatically presented by the system with a caution qualifier (e.g., “Proceed with caution”). The recommendation type remains **Go**, but its presentation and explanation are modified by the safety state. This preserves set containment while allowing state‐dependent advisory messaging.
canonical_change_proposal.proposed_wording: When S = CAUTION, any **Go** advisory generated by the active Layer 3 rule set is presented with a caution qualifier (e.g., “Proceed with caution”). The recommendation type remains **Go**, but its presentation and explanation are modified by the safety state. This preserves set containment while allowing state‐dependent advisory messaging.
canonical_change_proposal.diff_scope: One sentence, one clause replaced: 'the Go recommendation is automatically presented by the system' → 'any Go advisory generated by the active Layer 3 rule set is presented'.
canonical_change_proposal.authority_basis: OPEN-L3-3 resolution 2026-09-11; task §15 permits a minimal clarification when Resolution B is established and the existing sentence is genuinely misleading. The surface word 'automatically' created OPEN-L3-3 by leaving the wording readable as Interpretation A; the clarified wording removes that ambiguity while preserving the presentation-layer intent stated in the same paragraph and in architecture-illustration.md §202.
canonical_change_proposal.scientific_effect: None. RS_candidate(CAUTION) unchanged; no new rule; no rule removed. Go remains admissible in A_AI(CAUTION).
canonical_change_proposal.formal_effect: None. A_AI(CAUTION) = {Go, Delay} unchanged; containment relationships unchanged; Theorem C.2 and Theorem C.3 unchanged; Algorithm 3 and Algorithm 4 unchanged.
canonical_change_proposal.implementation_effect: Layer 3 engine implementation is unaffected. The presentation layer must, when rendering a Go advisory produced under S = CAUTION, attach a caution qualifier ('Proceed with caution' or equivalent). No Go emission mechanism outside the rule engine is required.
canonical_change_proposal.applied_notes: The clarification is minimal (one clause), preserves the intent stated in the same paragraph, and aligns Appendix C with the already-clear parallel text in architecture-illustration.md §202. Applied under task §15 permission after decomposition, chronology, and downstream-authority checks all converged on Interpretation B.
